input.command:
python -c "
import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel,ConstantModel
d=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv');x=d.shift_cm1.values;y=d.intensity.values
for lo,hi in [(200,300),(120,200),(300,370),(430,500),(540,1100)]:
    m=(x>lo)&(x<hi);print(lo,hi,y[m].mean(),y[m].std(),y[m].max(),x[m][y[m].argmax()])
for c,lo,hi in [(391.5,370,405),(415.1,405,435),(520.9,505,535)]:
    m=(x>lo)&(x<hi);mod=LorentzianModel()+ConstantModel()
    r=mod.fit(y[m],mod.make_params(amplitude=1e5,center=c,sigma=4,c=7500),x=x[m]);print(r.best_values,2*r.best_values['sigma'])
m=(x>380)&(x<425);print(np.round(y[m],0))
"

import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel,ConstantModel

for lo,hi in [(200,300),(120,200),(300,370),(430,500),(540,1100)]:
    m=(x>lo)&(x<hi);print(lo,hi,y[m].mean(),y[m].std(),y[m].max(),x[m][y[m].argmax()])
for c,lo,hi in [(391.5,370,405),(415.1,405,435),(520.9,505,535)]:
    m=(x>lo)&(x<hi);mod=LorentzianModel()+ConstantModel()
    r=mod.fit(y[m],mod.make_params(amplitude=1e5,center=c,sigma=4,c=7500),x=x[m]);print(r.best_values,2*r.best_values['sigma'])
m=(x>380)&(x<425);print(np.round(y[m],0))

candidates.evidence: Two sharp peaks at 391.3 and 415.3 cm-1 (separation ~24 cm-1) match the E2g(1)/A1g pair of few-layer to bulk MoS2 (E2g ~383-386, A1g ~405-408 cm-1; Lee et al. ACS Nano 2010). Both are blueshifted by ~6-8 cm-1 relative to typical values, so an offset or calibration or strain/doping effect is plausible and not excluded.
MoSe2 has A1g near 241 cm-1 and E2g near 287 cm-1, nothing there. Not supported.
The WSe2 E2g/A1g band (~250 cm-1) and 2LA(M) (~260 cm-1) are absent. No peak above noise appears between 200 and 370 cm-1.

input.hint_reasoning: WSe2 at 532 nm shows a near-degenerate E2g(Γ)/A1g(Γ) peak at ~249-252 cm-1, a 2LA(M) shoulder at ~260 cm-1, and weak features near 308 (B2g1, multilayer) and ~360-375 cm-1 (Zhao et al. Nanoscale 2013; Luo et al. Nanoscale 2013; Terrones et al. Sci. Rep. 2014). In this spectrum the 200-370 cm-1 region is flat. The scatter is about 130-180 counts, and the largest excursion is about 3-5% of the baseline of ~9400. The only sample peaks are at 391.3 and 415.3 cm-1, well above any WSe2 first-order mode (WSe2 phonon energies are lower because W and Se are heavy). The pair matches MoS2 in position and in the ~24 cm-1 spacing. The spectrum is therefore inconsistent with WSe2.

The 391/415 cm-1 positions are about 6-8 cm-1 higher than textbook MoS2. I cannot tell whether that is calibration, strain, doping, or a different material, so the MoS2 identification is likely but not certain.

The data cover 60-1100 cm-1 with the baseline around 7500-10000 counts and a rising background, so very weak WSe2 features cannot be strictly excluded. A real WSe2 sample would still show a strong ~250 cm-1 peak under these conditions, and it is absent.
Layer number cannot be reliably determined because the absolute mode positions look offset.
Resonance conditions (532 nm vs the WSe2 and MoS2 excitons) and any photoluminescence background are not characterised.
